title: Distance to a Cycle in Undirected Graph
summary: Given a connected undirected graph with exactly one cycle and containing n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, along with a 2D integer array representing the edges, return an integer array of size n.
statement: Given a connected undirected graph with exactly one cycle and containing n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, along with a 2D integer array representing the edges, return an integer array of size n. Each element in the array should represent the minimum distance from the corresponding node to any node within the cycle.
constraints: The connected undirected graph has n nodes and exactly one cycle.
Cycle nodes have distance zero; other nodes need their shortest edge distance to any cycle node.
Return one distance per node in numeric order.
hints: Repeatedly removing leaves exposes exactly the nodes on the unique cycle.
Prune degree-one nodes, then start a multi-source BFS from every unpruned node.
Mark cycle nodes distance zero and assign each unseen neighbor parent distance plus one.
A unicyclic graph’s non-cycle portion is a forest peeled completely by leaf pruning; multi-source BFS then gives shortest distance to the remaining cycle.
editorial: A unicyclic graph’s non-cycle portion is a forest peeled completely by leaf pruning; multi-source BFS then gives shortest distance to the remaining cycle.

tests.explanation: Nodes one through four form the cycle; the branches give distances [1,0,0,0,0,1,2].
Every node lies on the only cycle, so every distance is zero.
